cards.front: Stages of the nightly regression, trigger to signature mail.
cards.back: cron → limit check → sync → build flow → LSF submit → simulate → parse logs → merge coverage → signature mail → **release limit**. Know where the log is at each stage.
cards.author: claude

cards.front: The wrapper crashes after LSF submit. What releases the limit?
cards.back: Prove it from the script. If release only happens at the end, nothing does: the limit stays locked. Fixes: a `trap` on exit, a watchdog, or stale-lock detection.
cards.author: claude

cards.front: cron fires while last night's run is still going. What should happen?
cards.back: Decide **explicitly**: skip, queue or kill. Implement it with a lock file or PID check rather than relying on LSF side effects, then verify the behaviour.
cards.author: claude

cards.front: Why does a shelve regression need its base changelist?
cards.back: A shelve is a set of **changes relative to its base**, so it only applies cleanly onto that base.
cards.author: claude

cards.front: Why a release branch instead of mainline at a label?
cards.back: The milestone needs a **pinned version** that can still take targeted fixes while mainline moves on.
cards.author: claude

cards.front: Merging coverage from runs compiled from **different RTL**: what's the issue?
cards.back: The coverage models differ: bins or covergroups were added, removed or changed. A strict merge refuses or drops data. A flexible merge applies rules (e.g. union of items) so changed models can be combined.
cards.author: claude

cards.front: Why keep a .vdb retention and backup policy?
cards.back: Accumulated coverage is **expensive to regenerate**, and one deletion can wipe months.
cards.author: claude

cards.front: Name two concrete things that break when moving a flow from VCS to Xcelium.
cards.back: Compile, elaborate and run **switches** (different command-line options and flow), and **coverage database format/tools** (.vdb/URG vs the Xcelium coverage DB and tools). Also environment/bootenv and some PLI/DPI build details.
cards.author: claude
